content: For the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in adults, the recommended dosage of quinine sulfate is 648 mg, which corresponds to two capsules, administered orally every 8 hours for a duration of 7 days. It is advised that QUALAQUIN be taken with food to reduce the likelihood of gastric upset. In patients with acute uncomplicated malaria who also have severe chronic renal impairment, the recommended dosage regimen involves an initial loading dose of 648 mg of QUALAQUIN, followed 12 hours later by maintenance doses of 324 mg every 12 hours. The effects of mild and moderate renal impairment on the safety and pharmacokinetics of quinine sulfate have not been established. For patients with hepatic impairment, no adjustment to the recommended dose is necessary in cases of mild (Child-Pugh A) or moderate (Child-Pugh B) hepatic impairment. However, these patients should be closely monitored for potential adverse effects associated with quinine.
